correctness.rationale: For all a,b>0 and real states, direct substitution proves y(n+3)=ab*y(n+2)*y(n)^2, and the three initial y-values uniquely recover the full orbit. Zero entries become permanently zero in finite time. On nonzero orbits L=log(sqrt(ab)*|y|) obeys an exact linear recurrence with polynomial t^3-t^2-2 and spectrum r> s=sqrt(2/r)>1. The positive left eigenvector w produces log H and H(F)=H^r. The strict Perron mode gives extinction/escape. On H=1 the remaining conjugate pair is an expanding rotation with infinitely positive/negative scalar values unless all three initial logs vanish; that case is exactly eight preperiodic points. Log-triple norm growth forbids recurrence elsewhere; Poincare recurrence yields exactly convex combinations of three fixed masses. All quantifiers, boundaries and excluded c!=1 parameter regimes are stated; checker.py finite tests are supplementary.
